newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No increase in Australia air capacity to HK.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No increase in Australia air capacity to HK.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday that Australia and Hong Kong had failed to reach agreement on any increases in airline capacity and frequency in discussions here last Thursday.
Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said this was a particularly disappointing outcome given the strength of the Australia-Hong Kong market.
Sharp said the end-to-end market between the two countries grew 15 percent to 645,000 passengers in the 12 months to August 1996.
He said total traffic on the route, including traffic flying beyond Hong Kong, was approaching one million passengers a year and grew eight percent in 1995.

"It is difficult to understand why Hong Kong, with a commercially aggressive airline and the advantage of being at the centre of the fastest growing region in the world, should take the protectionist view about expanding capacity at this time," he said in a statement.
"An expanded air services agreement would demonstrate confidence in the future of Hong Kong beyond June 1997 (when the country returns to China)."
The last capacity increase in the Australia-Hong Kong market was agreed in November 1991 and the final phase of that increase became available in April 1995.
Australian airlines have been operating at their allocated limit since that time.
Sharp said discussions with Hong Kong would resume before the end of April next year.
The main airlines involved are Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Australia's Qantas Airways Ltd.
